newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe pledges tax cuts, further spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Juppe pledges tax cuts, further spending cuts.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe pledged on Tuesday to reduce social charges and income taxes in a speech outlining the centre-right coalition's platform for the May/June parliamentary election.

"We started in 1996 and 1997 to lower (social) charges by significant amounts, charges that weighed on the low paid and income taxes affecting millions of taxpayers," he told members of the coalition. "This programme of cuts already launched will be continued. It should be amplified."
But he said this pledge involved an obligation "to control and lower public spending" in France.
Juppe said it was necessary to lower charges on companies to encourage "a spirit of enterprise and free up initiative".
"Freeing up initiative involves as a priority easing the charges which, despite efforts undertaken, continue to suffocate business," he told the coalition members of the national assembly and senate.
"The French can no longer tolerate new taxes," he added. "The rigor which was forced on us to repay the debts run up by the Socialists is behind us."
The two-round election will be held on May 25 and June 1.
